scope: Retain newly supplied female AMH evidence for a future source-specific educational reference. No new clinical normal range, patient reference, interpolation or display geometry is activated.
authorization: The owner supplied the requested article and supplement and authorized work according to the plan. This review records source facts; it does not approve an unspecified new clinical profile.

citation.authors: Keyan Xu, Yehuan Yang et al.
citation.title: Age-specific anti-Müllerian hormone reference values using an ultrasensitive assay: Associations with ovarian aging and menopausal transition symptoms
citation.publicationStatus: Publisher-formatted original article, online publication; supplied PDF retains XX(XX) volume/issue placeholders.

provenance.reviewBasis: Read the complete supplied article; independently inspected workbook structure, published aggregate tables and embedded percentile figure. No refitting, new digitization or participant-level calculation.
sourceLoci: PDF pages 2–3: reference population, exclusions, assay, model and menopause definition
PDF page 4: Table 1 cohort ages and reference-model description
XLSX worksheet 2, Supplementary Table 1, A2:H7: five published percentile-estimate rows
XLSX supplementary figure 1: continuous percentile curves; embedded image labelled Figure 2
PDF pages 6–8 and XLSX Tables 9–10: separate menopausal-status analysis and unresolved inconsistencies
provenance.workbookClassification: Ten published aggregate tables and three embedded figures; no individual participant records, patient identifiers, LMS coefficients or model object.

referencePopulation.design: Community-based cross-sectional study; multistage stratified cluster sampling across 26 districts/counties in 12 provinces.
referencePopulation.menopauseStatus: Premenopausal. A separate 422-woman natural-postmenopause group was used for diagnostic comparison, not to construct the main age-reference curve.
referencePopulation.cycleSampling: Random day of the menstrual cycle.
exclusions: Oral contraceptive use or hormonal drug treatment in the preceding 30 days
AMH outlier more than 5 SD from the age-specific mean
notEstablished: This is not an explicitly PCOS-free cohort.
Rare observed ages 34 and 56 do not establish a numerical reference beyond the published 35–55 model.
Unknown menopause or treatment status must not be recoded as meeting the reference exclusions.
referencePopulation.separateLongitudinalCohort: The 2521-woman infertility cohort used conventional Kangrun AMH (LOD 0.01 ng/mL) and serial samples, not the HS-AMH population reference. Keep its eligibility and results separate.

assay.name: Diagnostic Kit for HS-AMH, Kangrun Biotech, Guangdong, China
assay.limitOfQuantification: Not reported separately in the supplied article/workbook; LOD must not be treated as LOQ.
assay.lowConcentrationPrecision: No numerical analytical CV or uncertainty near LOD supplied.
assay.belowLODModelHandling: No explicit substitution, exclusion or censored-likelihood procedure reported for GAMLSS fitting.
assay.crossMethodTransfer: No validated conversion to Access, Elecsys or other AMH platforms is established by this paper.

publishedReference.statistic: Author-published GAMLSS percentile estimates; p50 is a model median, not an arithmetic mean or a median recalculated from participant records.
publishedReference.tableHeading: Age-specific AMH percentile reference values by 5-year age bands (35–55 years)
publishedReference.ageSemantics: The heading says age bands, but AGE contains five scalar labels without interval boundaries/operators. The continuous source figure is consistent with model anchors at those age coordinates. Do not turn AGE 50 into a published constant median for ages 50–54.
publishedReference.modelDetailsAvailable: GAMLSS, stepwise comparison, AIC penalty k=2, R 4.3.3.
modelDetailsMissing: Selected distribution family and complete age-dependent coefficients
Single-year numerical table or executable author model
Explicit interpretation of the age-band wording
Detailed handling of measurements below LOD
publishedReference.precisionPolicy: Retain source decimals in evidence only. They do not imply equivalent clinical precision, especially p50 near LOD at age 55.
publishedReference.interpolationStatus: None implemented. A future interpolation through the five published anchors would be an explicitly reviewed application approximation, not a reconstruction of the unpublished full GAMLSS formula.

unresolvedSourceIssues.finding: Supplementary Table 2 group counts sum to 10497, while Total is 10543. The difference 46 equals the 4+42 participants outside 35–55 in the main table. This is a plausible explanation, not a confirmed reconstruction.
Supplementary Tables 9–10 contain 1346 premenopausal women aged 50–55, versus 1305 in main Table 1; the 41-person difference is unexplained.

unresolvedSourceIssues.issue: Below-LOD labels and reported postmenopausal median
unresolvedSourceIssues.finding: The no/yes labels in Supplementary Tables 9–10 run opposite to the main text and Figure 4. The figure depicts most postmenopausal values as undetectable, but text reports median 0.043 ng/mL above LOD 0.003 without saying whether the median excludes undetectable results. Do not swap labels or activate a postmenopausal median by assumption.

Secondary arithmetic from the four published Table 10 counts gives uncorrected Pearson chi-square about 196.787, whereas the article reports 38.6. The population/coding distinction is unresolved; no correction is inferred.

Main Tables 2 and 3 duplicate longitudinal cohort characteristics, despite a model-table cross-reference. Results say AMH alone is insufficient for diagnosing menopause, while stronger wording appears in the discussion. Neither supplies missing model parameters or validates a diagnostic feature.

recommendation.candidateScope: A future separate educational reference for premenopausal women aged 35–55, particularly the current gap after 45, with the source population and HS-AMH method stated.
beforeActivation: Resolve or explicitly qualify source age labels and application interpolation.
Define premenopausal and treatment eligibility without inferring menopause from age.
Clarify censoring and quantitative precision near LOD, particularly for the older-age endpoint.
Preserve the source median independently of the illustrative line and laboratory normal ranges.
notSupported: Automatic laboratory-normal-range replacement on other assays
Numerical extrapolation beyond age 55 or to late old age
An exact numerical patient marker for a result reported below LOD
recommendation.materialsStatus: Main article and SDC2 are now available; do not request them again. Author model tables/coefficients and clarification of censoring would resolve the remaining source gaps.
